column2: If you win, you live. If you lose, you die. That was the rule of the Cartel Olympics. Or so the story goes.
February ninth, 2023. Mauricio Morales says a cartel grabbed him off a Mexico City street, and he woke up in a windowless room.
Then the boss, Don Paco, noticed the Olympic rings tattooed on his wrist. Mau, he'd learn, was a famous runner.
Mexico's biggest cartels, Don Paco said, hold a secret tournament every year. Soccer. Boxing. Flag football. The bosses bet. The losers die.
Mau coached a flag football team. He says they won in overtime. He got a gold medal, and walked home at dawn.
A talent manager took it to Hollywood. Actor Michael Peña was interested, if a serious magazine would confirm it. So The Atlantic spent eight months checking.
The Mexican Olympic Committee had no record of him. And the photo of him racing at the Olympics? It showed an Italian runner.
Then there's February ninth. That's the day Mau was arrested for fraud, accused of taking about seven hundred thousand dollars with fake Beatles memorabilia.
He spent the next eighteen months in an ordinary Mexico City prison. And the reformed hit man who backed up his story? A fellow inmate.
The Cartel Olympics never happened. But the movie? Reportedly, it's back on.
